model: Alternative asset manager and insurer: Adjusted Net Income (FRE + insurance operating earnings + strategic holdings + realised investing earnings, after interest, preferred and tax) less SBC and balance-sheet reinvestment, capitalised at cost of equity with net debt held at zero (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_definition: LTM 2Q'26 Total Segment Earnings ($M): FRE 4,235.5 + Insurance Operating Earnings 1,121.2 + Strategic Holdings Operating Earnings 186.8 + Total Investing Earnings 1,095.1 (net realised performance income 703.5 + net realised investment income 391.6). Pre-interest, pre-preferred, pre-tax, after all cash compensation. Source: Q2 2026 earnings release (8-K 2026-07-30, EX-99.1 p.34 LTM reconciliation) and 10-Q for 2026-06-30 segment note.
inputs.sbc_source: Q2 2026 earnings release EX-99.1 p.34, LTM 2Q'26 GAAP-to-ANI reconciliation: equity-based compensation time-based 252.5 + performance-based 385.4 (Asset Management) + 102.1 (Insurance) = 740.0. These are the amounts KKR adds back to reach ANI; the house basis deducts them.
inputs.buyback_note: H1 2026 financing-activity repurchases per XBRL kpis (233.2); release p.30 reports $352M used 31-Dec-25 to 24-Jul-26 retiring 3.9M shares/awards at avg $90.87. FY2025 XBRL kpi shows only 3.4 which looks under-captured; not load-bearing since the count is held flat and SBC is expensed.
inputs.share_count_basis: KKR 'Adjusted Shares' at 30-Jun-2026: 897.78M common + 25.95M exchangeable securities (Arctos consideration) = 923.73M (release p.30). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so unvested awards are already charged. Series D mandatory convertible preferred (converts by 1-Mar-2028, ~$2.6B, ~18-22M shares at current prices) is NOT added to the count; instead its $161.7M/yr dividend is left inside the flows for the whole horizon as the economic proxy for that dilution (PV of the dividend at 10.5% ~ $1.5B vs ~$1.9B of shares at today's price -- slightly generous, disclosed).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 10.5% in USD: 10y UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.25 (KKR's 5y raw beta is ~1.5-1.6 but much of that is carry mark-to-market already captured by the scenario spread; charging it twice would stack risk). Single rate across scenarios per the risk-once rule. This is a levered-equity flow (after corporate interest and preferred dividends) so it is discounted at cost of equity, never WACC, and net debt is held at zero.
inputs.lease_treatment: None. Operating leases sit inside 'Other Operating Expenses' within FRE; no separate lease charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only: $16.2M LTM NCI on adjusted earnings is deducted inside the EBITDA-margin driver alongside net interest expense (305.7) and preferred dividends (161.7), so FY0 NOPAT ties to reported ANI of 5,022.4.
inputs.net_debt_rationale: Held at ZERO. The flow is post-interest (FCFE-style), so subtracting KKR & Co.'s $9.3B par debt would deduct it twice. Symmetrically, the $5.3B AM-segment cash and $8.6B AM-segment investments ($4.6B net cash and investments, release p.28) are NOT added to the bridge because the income they produce (realised investment income, dividends) is already inside Total Segment Earnings -- matching-asset rule. Global Atlantic's debt and reserves are operating liabilities of the insurer and never enter the bridge; GA book value $11.8B. Unmodelled cushion: $2.6B embedded unrealised AM gains and $2.5B net unrealised carried interest (after 75% comp accrual) are not in the flows beyond the LTM realisation run-rate.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: KKR is an alternative asset manager (PE, credit, infrastructure, real assets; $796B AUM) that also consolidates a ~$220B-AUM annuity/life insurer (Global Atlantic). The XBRL consolidated GAAP lines are unusable for an owner-FCF DCF: 'revenue' includes consolidated-fund gains and GA policy economics, OCF swings from -$7.7B to +$6.6B with fund consolidation, and there is no capex or EBITDA. The routing table has no asset-manager row; the closest rows are 'insurer/holdco (BVPS x P/B)' and the FCFE-at-cost-of-equity precedent used for NAB.AX/GL/IAG.AX/GMG.AX/CHC.AX. BVPS compounding is wrong here because most of KKR's value is a capital-light fee stream, not book. So the model discounts KKR's own Adjusted Net Income -- the distributable, post-interest, post-tax segment measure -- via the engine: base_revenue = Total Segment Earnings; ebitda_margin = 1 - (net interest + preferred dividends + NCI)/TSE; sbc_pct = equity comp add-backs (house basis charges them); da_pct = 0 (D&A ~$81M is already inside TOE); capex_pct = balance-sheet reinvestment (capital KKR retains to fund Strategic Holdings acquisitions, co-investments and GA capital; the growth path assumes the returns on it); cash_tax_rate = income taxes on adjusted earnings / pre-tax adjusted earnings (18.4% LTM). Street basis (SBC added back) = ANI as KKR reports it. The insurance segment is valued inside the same stream at its operating earnings (spread income after cost of insurance and G&A), which is the right flow for a spread-based annuity writer; it is NOT separately valued on book because GA's earnings are consolidated into ANI and its capital is not distributable to KKR shareholders. The split is disclosed (IOE ~17% of TSE). FY0 is the LTM to 30-Jun-2026 rather than FY2025 because FRE is compounding at ~19% and a Dec-25 base would be three quarters stale. Price is a regular-session close, not after-hours.

historical_growth.series_note: GAAP CSV lines are meaningless for this business (see inputs.notes). 'Revenue' below = Total Segment Earnings; 'FCF' = Adjusted Net Income; 'EPS' = ANI per adjusted share; 'Equity' = GAAP total shareholders' equity incl. NCI and Global Atlantic (from the CSV). Segment history from the FY2025 10-K three-year segment note and Q2 2026 release: FRE 2,383.8 / 3,267.8 / 3,714.3 (FY23/24/25), LTM 4,235.5; TSE 4,155.3 / 5,509.5 / 5,890.3, LTM 6,638.6; ANI ~3,077 (FY23, from the FY2023 release, $3.42/sh) / 4,202.3 / 4,377.5, LTM 5,022.4; IOE 816.6 / 1,014.5 / 1,109.4, LTM 1,121.2; SH OE 14.5 / 76.2 / 162.1, LTM 186.8. The '3yr' figures are FY2023 -> LTM 2Q'26 (2.5 years) because the pre-2023 segment history is not in the extracted corpus (Extracted/ is empty on this XBRL-path filer).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Year-1 base-case growth in Total Segment Earnings: FRE (64% of TSE) guided to continued double-digit growth and running +19% LTM, insurance operating earnings +9%, investing earnings held near the LTM run-rate. Blends to ~12%, below the 20.6% trailing CAGR because FY2023 was a realisation trough and the FY2024 GA buy-in inflated the base.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: GAAP equity CAGR (12.6% 3yr / 14.1% 5yr) diverges >30% from segment-earnings CAGR (20.6%) and ANI-per-share CAGR (21.5%). Expected: GAAP equity includes NCI and Global Atlantic's AOCI-laden book and was reset by the Jan-2024 GA 100% acquisition; it is not the compounding base for this business.
historical_growth.notes: SBC (equity comp add-backs) grew from 616.9 (FY2023) to 740.0 (LTM), 6.3%/yr, well below ANI growth -- SBC is falling as a share of earnings (14.5% -> 11.1% of TSE), so the house/street gap is narrowing, not widening.

base.growth_note: TSE growth: FRE +15-16% Y1-2 fading to high-single by Y5 as fee-paying AUM growth normalises from +15% toward +8%; IOE +8% fading to +4%; investing earnings flat at the LTM $1.1B run-rate (no re-rating of the realisation cycle either way); SH OE climbing toward management's $1.1B-by-2030 target. Blended 12% -> 3.5%.
base.margin_note: EBITDA-margin driver = 1 - (net interest expense + preferred dividends + NCI)/TSE. FY0 = 1 - (305.7+161.7+16.2)/6,638.6 = 92.72%. Fixed charges assumed to grow ~5%/yr (KKR keeps issuing long-dated paper for growth; preferred dividend kept as the dilution proxy) while TSE grows faster, so the ratio drifts up to 94.5%.
base.capex_note: Balance-sheet reinvestment: cash retained to fund Strategic Holdings acquisitions (~20 businesses, target OE $350M FY26 -> $1.1B 2030), fund co-investments/GP commitments and any GA capital. 20% of TSE ($1.3B) in Y1 fading to 11% as growth slows. KKR retains ~$3.8B/yr after the $0.78 dividend, so this charges roughly a third of retained cash as growth capital and treats the rest as distributable.
base.tax_note: Income taxes on adjusted earnings / pre-tax adjusted earnings = 1,132.7 / 6,155.4 = 18.4% LTM, drifting to 20% as the carried-interest and Section 199A benefits are assumed to erode modestly.

bull.growth_note: Management's 'double the firm twice in a decade' ambition roughly delivered: FRE +20%+ for three years on K-Series wealth flows, Helix digital-infrastructure and asset-based finance; realisation cycle reopens so investing earnings grow with AUM; GA + Ivy sidecars scale insurance economics; SH OE reaches $1.1B by 2030. Heavier reinvestment (22% of TSE) funds it.

bear.growth_note: The 2026 private-credit stress narrative becomes real: credit losses in the GA general account and KKR credit funds, LP allocations to alternatives pause, realisations dry up so investing earnings roughly halve from $1.1B, FRE growth drops to mid-single digits on fee pressure and slower fundraising, GA spread compresses as rates fall. TSE dips ~1% over three years then recovers at 4-5%. Fixed charges (interest, preferred) stay while earnings fall so the margin driver drops; equity comp does not flex down; tax rate rises on carried-interest reform.

scenario_narratives.base: KKR compounds Total Segment Earnings at 12% fading to 3.5% over ten years. Fee Related Earnings -- 64% of the base and the durable engine -- keep growing double-digit for three years as flagship vintages (North America XIV, Infrastructure V), K-Series wealth vehicles and Global Atlantic's captive assets lift fee-paying AUM, then normalise toward high-single digits. Insurance operating earnings grow with the GA/Ivy book at 8% fading to 4%. Realised carry and investment income are held at the LTM $1.1B run-rate -- neither a boom nor a drought -- and Strategic Holdings dividends climb toward management's 2030 target. Fixed charges (net interest, Series D preferred, NCI) grow slower than earnings, the adjusted tax rate drifts from 18.4% to 20%, and 20% fading to 11% of TSE is retained each year as growth capital. The house basis charges equity compensation (11% of TSE, drifting to 9.5%) that KKR adds back in its own ANI.
scenario_narratives.bull: The wealth channel and insurance flywheel deliver management's stated ambition to roughly double the firm twice in a decade: FRE grows 18-20% for three years on K-Series inflows, Helix digital infrastructure ($10B initial capital), asset-based finance and Arctos; the monetisation cycle reopens so investing earnings scale with AUM; GA plus the Ivy sidecars push insurance economics past $3B; and Strategic Holdings reaches $1.1B of operating earnings by 2030. Heavier balance-sheet reinvestment (22% of TSE) funds it, the terminal multiple is 22x and terminal growth 3.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2026 'private credit meltdown' narrative turns into losses: credit impairments in Global Atlantic's general account and KKR's credit funds, LP allocations to alternatives stall, exits dry up so realised carry roughly halves, FRE growth falls to mid-single digits on fee pressure and slower fundraising, and falling rates compress GA's spread. Total Segment Earnings dip about 1% over three years before recovering at 4-5%. Fixed charges and equity compensation do not flex down, so margins fall; carried-interest tax reform lifts the adjusted rate to 22%; the terminal multiple is 15x. Balance-sheet leverage at both KKR and GA means the equity absorbs the whole earnings shortfall.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 25%: KKR is a levered financial with a $220B-AUM annuity writer inside it, ~16% of segment earnings are realisation-dependent, and the 2026 private-credit quality concern is a live, sector-wide risk rather than a hypothetical. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (wealth-channel flows, a reopened exit cycle, GA spread holding, SH execution to $1.1B). Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value KKR on what it can actually distribute -- Adjusted Net Income after interest, preferred dividends and tax -- rather than on consolidated GAAP cash flow, which is dominated by consolidated funds and the insurance general account. The house basis charges the ~$740M/yr of equity compensation KKR adds back and retains a share of earnings as growth capital; the street basis is KKR's own ANI. Discount at cost of equity, hold net debt at zero (the flow is already post-interest), and give no credit in the bridge for the $4.6B of AM-segment net cash and investments, the $2.6B embedded gains or the $2.5B net unrealised carry, since their income is already in the flows at the LTM realisation rate. Global Atlantic is valued through its operating earnings inside the same stream, not on book.
key_risks_to_valuation: Realised carry and investment income (~$1.1B LTM, 16% of TSE) are lumpy; holding them flat is a modelling convention, not a forecast -- a two-year exit drought is the bear case
Global Atlantic credit losses, reserve strengthening or spread compression flow straight into insurance operating earnings; GA leverage is inside the equity
Fee-paying AUM growth (+15% LTM) is the single most important driver; LP allocation pauses or fee-rate pressure would cut the FRE path

The balance-sheet reinvestment charge (20% of TSE fading to 11%) is a judgment; charging the full ~$3.8B/yr KKR actually retains would cut the base value by roughly a third, charging nothing would lift it by a similar amount
Series D preferred conversion (by Mar-2028) is proxied by leaving its dividend in the flows; if the stock rises the conversion is less dilutive than the proxy, and vice versa
Carried-interest and Section 199A tax treatment: the 18.4% adjusted tax rate could step up to the mid-20s under reform
